name: RocksDB
tagline: Meta's embeddable LSM-tree key-value engine, the storage layer under dozens of databases.
description: RocksDB is a C++ library for persistent, ordered key-value storage built on a log-structured merge tree and tuned for fast SSDs. Meta forked it from LevelDB in 2012 to add multi-threaded compaction, column families, transactions, rich tuning options and much better write throughput, and it has since become the default building block for storage engines: MyRocks, TiKV, Kafka Streams and Flink state, CockroachDB before Pebble, and many more. It is not a server; you embed it and own the API on top. Expect a large configuration surface, and budget time to understand compaction styles and write amplification.

scale.notes: Single-process library; multi-terabyte instances per node are common, and distribution is left to the system embedding it.

strengths: High write throughput from an LSM design with parallel compaction
Column families, merge operators, compaction filters and prefix bloom filters
Optimistic and pessimistic transactions with snapshots
Huge production footprint at Meta and inside many databases
Extensive tuning knobs for leveled, universal and FIFO compaction
weaknesses: Very large configuration surface; defaults rarely fit demanding workloads
Write and space amplification from compaction must be managed
Only C++, C and Java APIs are first-party
Not a database server: no networking, replication or query language
useCases: Storage engine for a custom database or service
Write-heavy local indexes and caches on SSD
notIdealFor: Teams wanting a ready-made database server
Read-mostly workloads where a B-tree like LMDB is simpler
